in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you tell me **how many children** you're inquiring about, and what are their **names and ages**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To help determine your eligibility, I need to ask: **Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Before I can properly assess your situation, I need to check the specific rules about this. Let me look up the guidance on Child Benefit eligibility when a child lives with someone else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting while I checked the rules. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to ask a few more questions to establish whether you could still be eligible.

**Are you making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep** (such as paying for clothes, food, pocket money, or helping with housing costs)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently contributing anything financially towards Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules for Child Benefit:

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not making any financial contributions towards his upkeep, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

According to the rules, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child, which means either:
- You live with them, OR
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them

Since neither of these conditions apply in your case, you unfortunately would not meet the eligibility criteria.

However, if your circumstances change in the future and you do start contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep at a level equal to or greater than the Child Benefit amount, you would then be able to claim. In that case, you should contact the Child Benefit Office to make a claim.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
No, that's clear. Thank you for explaining it to me.
